title: Fix operator leader-election deadlock during VPC cluster upgrades causing node-agent roll stalls
creator: Ava Nakamura
description: Summary: Multiple Private/VPC customers experienced stalled node-agent rollouts and Helm upgrade hang during operator v1.9.2 -> v1.9.3 upgrades. Symptoms included operator pods alternating between Running and CrashLoopBackOff, control-plane reconciliation stalls, and customer traffic degradation for workloads pinned to upgraded nodes. This ticket tracks triage, immediate mitigation (hotfix), customer notifications, and follow-up work to prevent recurrence.
reproduction_steps: 1) Customer runs helm upgrade for redwood-operator from 1.9.2 to 1.9.3 in a VPC cluster with >100 custom resources.
2) Helm post-upgrade hooks start; operator attempts to re-establish leader election across namespaces using ConfigMap lock implementation.
3) ConfigMap-based locking experiences transient update collisions (ownerReferences + automated controller patches) resulting in repeated leader flapping.

4) Operator's reconciliation loop schedules simultaneous node-agent daemonset rollouts; KV cache invalidation leads to repeated large-scale reconciling and API throttling; pods stall and some enter CrashLoopBackOff.
5) Observed customer impact: control-plane 95th latency spikes, rollout progress stalls for >30m, support escalations from 2 enterprise customers.

initial_triage_notes: 03/09 18:35 - Oncall (Diego) paged, started live debugging with Customer Support and Solutions.
03/09 18:50 - Replicated in internal staging by running helm upgrade on a large synthetic CR set; reproduced leader flapping and rollout stall.
03/09 19:20 - Determined primary failure vector: ConfigMap-based leader election in multi-namespace operator combined with Helm post-upgrade annotation churn.
03/09 19:45 - Classified as P0 due to customer-facing service degradation and multiple escalations.
root_cause: The operator's previous leader-election implementation uses a namespaced ConfigMap lock which becomes contended when Helm post-upgrade hooks modify the same ConfigMap metadata (ownerReferences/annotations). The resulting update conflicts trigger rapid leader loss and reacquisition attempts. This, combined with a large-scale, synchronous node-agent rollout that invalidates shared KV caches, causes reconciliation thrashing and API server throttling.
immediate_decision: Ship a targeted hotfix that switches leader-election to use coordination.k8s.io Lease objects (non-namespaced semantics) and tightens retry backoff to avoid immediate re-election storms. Additionally, include a Helm post-upgrade ordering hook to gracefully transfer leadership before resource mutation and add a temporary guard that sequences large daemonset rollouts with a safe concurrency window.

canary_plan: Phase 1: Apply operator-1.9.3-hotfix to internal staging with 200 synthetic CRs. Validate leader stability for 1h under helm upgrade churn.
Phase 2: Canary rollout to Customer A (non-critical prod) and Customer B (dedicated capacity) during maintenance window; monitor console latency and rollout progress.
Phase 3: Gradual expansion to remaining affected customers with automated rollback on >3% pod crash rate or >20m stalled rollouts.
testing_and_qc: Added integration tests that simulate Helm hook annotation churn and verify leader survives (operator/e2e/leader-election-test).
Load test: 10k reconciliation events per minute to verify API error budgets remain within SLO.
QA checklist attached to PR 1142 and 1143; security sign-off not required for this hotfix but runtime team to run a quick smoke test for RBAC changes.

postmortem_notes: Preliminary postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-17. Will include timeline, root cause analysis, why preflight checks did not catch ownerReference churn, and recommendations for product-level safeguards.
Initial remediation reduces blast radius during upgrades; long-term fix is to remove cross-namespace ConfigMap locks across all operator builds.
